name: cable-input
title: Input on a long lead: pull-up, series resistor and capacitor, TVS at the connector
about: A button, reed contact or open-collector sensor at the end of a long lead, read by an MCU input. A TVS at the connector takes ESD off the line; a 4.7 kΩ pull-up holds the line high against what the lead picks up; 1 kΩ in series and 100 nF to ground form a low-pass at the pin and limit the current into the pin's protection diodes while the TVS clamps (maker-coverage BL-12, HT-1, CK-16).

ports.in: the filtered signal – to the MCU input (one with a Schmitt trigger)
ports.vcc: the logic supply of that input (3.3 V; up to 5.0 V – the TVS's working voltage)
ports.gnd: ground – also the return wire of the lead

components.label: {as}: lead (JST PH, pin 1 = signal, pin 2 = GND)
components.notes: Its wires go to the button or sensor, not to another board of the project (off_board).

components.label: {as}: ESD protection at the connector (TVS 5 V)
components.notes: Bidirectional; next to J1, its ground pad short to J1's ground pin.

nets.name: line
nets.notes: The wire side: connector, TVS, pull-up.

notes: Pull-up 4.7 kΩ: a design choice inside the '10 kΩ or less' for inputs on long leads (HINT.cable_line, maker-coverage HT-1) – about 0.7 mA through the contact at 3.3 V. It sits on the wire side, so the contact current does not flow through R2.

Series 1 kΩ: between the TVS and the pin. While the TVS clamps (VC 11.6 V at 5 A, 8/20 µs – LRC LESD5D5.0CT1G, p. 2) it keeps the current into the pin's protection diodes near 8 mA for those microseconds; it is the series resistance REQ.missing/leave asks for (CK-16; the emonTx uses 1 kΩ and a TVS).

100 nF with R2: the falling edge (contact closes) with τ = 1 kΩ × 100 nF = 0.1 ms, the rising edge with (4.7 k + 1 k) × 100 nF = 0.57 ms. It removes spikes, not contact bounce (milliseconds): debounce in the firmware (HINT.debounce). For pulses faster than about 1 kHz (flow sensor, anemometer) a smaller capacitor.
The RC makes slow edges: read it with an input that has a Schmitt trigger enabled; a plain CMOS input may toggle several times while the edge passes its threshold.

TVS LESD5D5.0CT1G: working voltage 5.0 V, leakage ≤ 1 µA at 5.0 V – less than 5 mV across the pull-up. On a 5 V rail that reaches 5.25–5.5 V the working voltage is exceeded (LIM.v holds a TVS to VRWM without margin): take a TVS with VRWM ≥ 5.5 V there. It is bidirectional; its SPICE model is one junction, right while the line stays between 0 V and VCC.

J1 is marked off_board: REQ.missing/leave then checks that a resistor stands between the wire and the MCU pin. For a lead to another board of the project, model it as a cable in the graph instead – HINT.cable_line names its net.
A sensor that needs a supply wants a third wire and its own feed (and a fuse or resistor in it) – not in this block.
sim.json: the in net under the MCU's inputs. The contact is off the board and not simulated; closed, the line and the input sit at 0 V and the pull-up carries the 0.7 mA.
